originalTitle: Australia news live: police locate parents of toddler found wandering Sydney street alone at 2am
content: Beetaloo gas set to flow in NT, despite environmental concerns The first gas from the controversial Beetaloo Basin fracking projects in Australia’s north is set to flow to homes and businesses in a territory touting its vast energy supply potential, AAP reports. The basin is a major onshore shale gas resource in the Northern Territory’s Sturt Plateau, about 500km southeast of Darwin. On Tuesday, first gas is set to flow, with more than 40 terajoules a day going into the territory’s gas grid. The territory uses about 60 terajoules a day of gas at peak levels for power generation and mines. NT chief minister Lia Finocchiaro said: Every time Territorians flick on a light switch, or pull a cold beer from the fridge, they’ll see the benefits of the Beetaloo Basin at work. Beetaloo fracking, construction of pipelines to get the gas to market, and using the gas to power AI datacentres have all been vigorously opposed by environmental groups. Fracking could see up to 6,000 wells drilled through underground water supplies, which supply 90% of the territory’s water needs, Environment Centre NT acting chief executive Bree Ahrens said: Water is life in the territory and we are calling for a ban on fracking and AI data centres before it’s too late. NSW police have located the parents of a toddler found wandering the road alone just after 2am this morning. Official initially issued a public appeal for information after the young child was found in Ramsgate, a suburb in southern Sydney, without his parents or carers. He was thought to be about two years old. Police said just before 8am that his parents had been found. An official said: Police would like to thank everyone who shared our appeal. Inquiries are continuing into the incident. Continuing on from the last post … Dowling, who told estimates she first met Hutley when she came to the bar in 1997, said she knew “most of the senior members of the inner bar after 30 years in Sydney”. Asked if she and Hutley were friends, she said: I know him professionally and socially and have utter respect for his professionalism, and if Mr Hutley considered that he had some kind of conflict that meant that he shouldn’t accept that from the attorney general, I have total confidence that he would have informed the attorney general of that. She said her signing a statement of support for Hutley’s candidacy for the NSW bar council in 2015 did not give rise to a conflict, saying she was one of 26 other barristers who signed the letter “ten years ago”. She said none of the names were interstate lawyers. Asked if it would have been more appropriate for someone from interstate to write the review, she said: It’s a matter for the attorney general whom he seeks advice from. On Monday morning, Daley told estimates he rejected the suggestion that Dowling and Hutley were friends. He said he had “full and absolute confidence” in Dowling and that Hutley’s review had provided “an objective and expert analysis of [the report’s] shortcomings”. NSW state’s top prosecutor discussed barristers to review findings against her office The NSW director of public prosecutions (DPP), Sally Dowling, says she discussed a list of barristers to lead an independent review into controversial findings against her office with the NSW attorney general, before he appointed someone she had known “personally and professionally” for nearly 30 years. Last month, a parliamentary committee voted 4-3 to find Dowling had given false evidence about the pitching of a story about an Indigenous child performing an acknowledgement of country at a sentencing hearing to radio station 2GB. Dowling admitted her office had pitched the story, but denied she had authorised it. Daley and the DPP rejected the committee’s findings. At budget estimates on Monday, Dowling said that she and the NSW attorney general, Michael Daley, had spoken before Noel Hutley SC was appointed to lead an independent review, which found there was “no positive basis” to find she had given false evidence. Dowling said: The attorney [general] called me to tell me that he was appointing a senior counsel to review the evidence that was before the inquiry and its report of the majority. He raised quite a number of [senior counsel’s] names that he was considering, including Mr Hutley’s name, and some of those people did have a conflict, they had acted for the ODPP, for me, and that was about the extent of the discussion. She said Daley had not asked for “advice”. “He mentioned some names, and I responded to those names,” she said. Dowling said of the list of eight to 12 people, she said two “would not be appropriate”, but she did not raise Hutley as inappropriate as she did not believe there was a conflict of interest. Under further questioning, Dowling said she had indicated to Daley that she knew Hutley, but had not given any further detail. Here’s a dispatch from our reporter Cait Kelly in Nepal Border area between Nepal and China where 33 Australians are missing still almost entirely cut off Guardian Australia’s Cait Kelly has another dispatch from Nepal. She writes: It has been almost a week since the catastrophic floods in Nepal and not even a vehicle can get into the area where the majority of missing Australians were last heard from. Gyirong Port, the border area between Nepal and China, was the first to be hit. Images from Chinese rescue teams who have managed to get in by helicopter or hiking show the area has been completely flattened. The immigration building, the power lines, everything, just wiped away. News that phone connectivity to the area was back on spread quickly on Monday around the families of lost Australians who have come to Kathmandu to wait. In WhatsApp groups and over Facebook, they shared any updates they had. chineseTitle: 澳大利亚新闻直播：凌晨 2 点，警方找到了在悉尼街头独自徘徊的幼儿的父母
chineseContent: 尽管存在环境问题，Beetaloo 天然气仍将在北领地流入 据 AAP 报道，澳大利亚北部备受争议的 Beetaloo 盆地水力压裂项目的第一批天然气将流向该地区的家庭和企业，该地区吹捧其巨大的能源供应潜力。该盆地是北领地 Sturt 高原的主要陆上页岩气资源，位于达尔文东南约 500 公里处。周二，第一批天然气将开始输送，每天有超过 40 太焦耳的天然气进入该地区的天然气管网。该地区每天在峰值水平下使用约 60 太焦耳的天然气用于发电和采矿。北领地首席部长 Lia Finocchiaro 表示：每当北领地人打开电灯开关，或者从冰箱里拿出一杯冰镇啤酒时，他们都会看到 Beetaloo Basin 在工作中带来的好处。 Beetaloo 水力压裂、建设将天然气推向市场的管道以及使用天然气为人工智能数据中心提供动力都遭到了环保组织的强烈反对。水力压裂可以通过地下水钻探多达 6,000 口井，满足该地区 90% 的用水需求，北领地环境中心代理首席执行官 Bree Ahrens 表示：“水是该地区的生命，我们呼吁在为时已晚之前禁止水力压裂和人工智能数据中心。”今天凌晨两点刚过，新南威尔士州警方找到了一名被发现独自在路上徘徊的幼儿的父母。这名年幼的孩子在悉尼南部郊区拉姆斯盖特被发现，没有他的父母或照顾者，官方最初公开呼吁提供信息。据认为他大约两岁。警方称，就在上午 8 点之前，他的父母被发现了。一名官员表示：警方感谢所有与我们分享呼吁的人。事件的调查仍在继续。继续上一篇文章……道林，谁
